opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and as an Analyst he does not own the system, so admin is not permitted. Per policy, full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system. Recommend granting write (the maximum allowed).
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E025 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full-time — discrepancy). As a contractor, max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested admin is above max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Michael Cervantes (E025) requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. The Security note shows E025 is a contractor with basic security training, which limits access to read (write requires advanced training; contractor never admin). The HR note claims full-time, which would allow write at most — a discrepancy exists. Since admin is never permitted and the facts conflict, I grant the most restrictive valid maximum: read. This is at/below the requested level and complies with policy.
